The Cambodia Relocation Guide

The easiest country in the region to stay in legally, and the one where that is changing fastest. Every route, with the 2026 enforcement shift built in.

Edition v1.0.0 Verified September 8, 2026 Next review December 8, 2026 8 pathways 23 cited sources Navigator edition

Read this before you rely on anything here. This is researched reference material, not legal or tax advice, and no lawyer-client relationship is created by buying it. Immigration rules change without notice and are applied with discretion by individual officers. Every claim is numbered to a source you can check yourself, and each source is labelled with how much weight it carries.

Navigator edition. This guide was researched against public primary and government sources by its publisher. No licensed practitioner in Cambodia has reviewed it, and we do not pretend otherwise. That is exactly why every pathway carries its own verify-this-yourself steps, naming the office that can answer, the question to ask, and what a real answer sounds like. Run them. They cost an hour and they are worth more than our assurance.

Everything here was verified on September 8, 2026. Before you spend money or book a flight, confirm the specific rule against the cited source or with a licensed Vietnamese immigration adviser. Cambodia is effectively dollarized. US dollars are the working currency for rent, salaries, visas, and most retail; Cambodian riel is used mainly as small change at roughly 4,000 KHR to US$1. This removes an entire category of currency friction that Vietnam has, and it is one of the genuine practical advantages of moving here. Note the flip side: worn, torn, or pre-2009 US notes are routinely refused.

Start here: what is not true

Six beliefs that cost Americans the most money on the way to Cambodia. We lead with these because the expensive mistakes happen before anyone files a form.

Widely believedAn apostille will work for my documents, like it does everywhere else.

Actually: No. Cambodia is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, so an apostille is not accepted. US documents need the full three-step chain: Secretary of State certification for state-issued documents, then US Department of State authentication, then legalization by the Cambodian Embassy. This is the single most expensive misunderstanding on this list, because getting an apostille feels like doing it right. 215

Why the myth persists: Most countries joined the Convention and most guidance is written for them. Vietnam itself joined with effect from 11 September 2026, which makes the contrast even more confusing for anyone comparing the two.

Widely believedThe business visa lets me work.

Actually: It does not. Cambodia runs a two-document system: the EB extension from the Ministry of Interior gives you the right to stay, and a separate work permit from the Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training gives you the right to work. Holding EB while working without a permit is illegal employment, and 2026 has brought more frequent compliance checks at businesses and substantial fines. 1112

Why the myth persists: It is called a business visa, everyone calls it a business visa, and for years nobody checked.

Widely believedCambodia is the place where you just show up forever and nobody asks questions.

Actually: That was substantially true and is becoming less so. The ordinary E-class visa really is extendable indefinitely, which is genuinely rare. But in 2026 extensions increasingly require real supporting documents — employment proof, company papers, accommodation records — and twelve-month extensions require a sponsor. The mechanism is still the most permissive in the region; the paperwork behind it is no longer optional. 1011

Why the myth persists: The reputation was earned over fifteen years and reputations lag reality by several years.

Widely believedI can buy land or a house in Cambodia.

Actually: Foreigners cannot own land. You can own a condominium unit under a strata title, but only on the first floor or above, and only within a cap of 70% of the units in that building. For landed property the routes are a long-term lease, a Cambodian-majority company, or a licensed trustee under the 2019 Trust Law. Nominee arrangements — putting the land in a Cambodian friend's name — are common, and they are exactly as risky as they sound. 20

Why the myth persists: Property is marketed hard to foreigners, and the distinction between a strata-titled condo and everything else is not something a sales agent volunteers.

Widely believedCambodia doesn't tax foreign income, so I'm free and clear.

Actually: This is genuinely disputed, and this guide will not pretend otherwise. Professional sources state that residents — anyone present more than 182 days — are taxed on worldwide salary at progressive rates up to 20%. Other sources describe a system that in practice reaches only Cambodian-sourced income. See the contested-claims section: the law and the enforcement pattern point in different directions, and the honest answer is that you are choosing which risk to accept. 161718

Why the myth persists: Both descriptions are repeated confidently by people who have never been assessed either way.

Widely believedCitizenship by investment is a $245,000 fast track and basically a formality.

Actually: The program is real, unlike Vietnam's much-hyped golden visa — but the headline number is not the cost. A US$245,000 donation to the government or a US$305,000 qualifying investment is the entry ticket; all-in costs including fees run to roughly US$330,000 or more per applicant, and you must travel to Cambodia three times during the process. The regulatory framework is also actively evolving. 19

Why the myth persists: Citizenship-by-investment marketing quotes the donation and omits the fees, exactly as property marketing quotes the unit price and omits the taxes.

Your pathway, in questions

Answer honestly rather than optimistically. Every answer narrows to exactly one route, including the routes that turn out not to exist. You can go back at any point.

    The pathways in full

    Every legal route, whether or not the tree sent you there. Read your own first, then read the one you would fall back to.

    Tourist (T-class) Visa

    T low

    Thirty days, extendable once by thirty days, then you must leave. Cheaper than the ordinary visa and a dead end by design. Correct for a holiday, wrong for anything else.

    Best for
    Genuine tourism of under two months, with no intention to return long-term.
    You get
    30 days, extendable once by 30 days
    Renewable
    No — a single 30-day extension, then exit.
    Work locally
    No.
    Family
    Each traveller applies individually.
    Toward permanent residence
    No.
    Realistic timeline
    On arrival at the counter, or roughly 3 business days for the e-visa.

    Verify this yourself before spending money

    Under an hour of work. This is the check that matters — not our word, and not an agency's.

    The current tourist visa fee and whether your nationality can get it on arrival

    Ask: Cambodian General Department of Immigration

    Open the official e-visa portal directly and read the fee and eligibility page before booking flights. www.evisa.gov.kh

    A real answer sounds like: A published fee on a .gov.kh domain. Any site charging a large 'service fee' on top is a reseller.

    Hard requirements

    • US passport valid at least 6 months with a blank page — Standard across all Cambodian visa classes. 1
    • Passport photo — Bring physical photos as well as digital — on-arrival counters still ask for paper.

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    Tourist visa on arrival or e-visaAbout US$30 plus e-visa processingConfirm the current figure on the official portal; on-arrival and online prices differ slightly. 1

    Step by step

    1. Decide honestly whether you are a tourist

      If there is any chance you will stay past two months, buy the ordinary E-class visa instead. The price difference is about five dollars and it is the difference between a dead end and an open door. 10

      Who: You

    2. Apply online or on arrival

      The official e-visa portal is a government site. As in Vietnam, search results are full of resellers. 1

      Who: You

    3. Extend once if you need to, then leave

      A single 30-day extension is available. After that the class is exhausted.

      Who: You Where: General Department of Immigration

    How this goes wrong

    Taking the tourist visa to save a few dollars, then deciding to stay

    Consequence: You must exit the country and re-enter on an ordinary visa. A flight and two days lost, for a five-dollar saving.

    Avoid it: If in any doubt, take the ordinary E-class visa. It is the single most consequential five dollars in this guide.

    Assuming the tourist visa extends indefinitely like the ordinary one

    Consequence: Overstay, at a daily fine, plus an exit problem.

    Avoid it: One extension only. Diarise the exit date on arrival.

    Ordinary (E-class) Visa — the gateway

    E low

    The most useful document in Cambodian immigration and the reason people call this the easiest country in the region. Thirty days on arrival, and then — uniquely — convertible into an extension of stay that can be renewed indefinitely. Almost every long-term route in this guide starts here.

    Best for
    Everyone staying beyond a month, including people who have not yet decided what they are doing.
    You get
    30 days on entry, then converted to an EB, EG, ER, or ES extension of 1, 3, 6, or 12 months
    Renewable
    Yes, indefinitely, through repeated extensions.
    Work locally
    The visa and extension give the right to stay. Work requires a separate work permit.
    Family
    Each person needs their own visa and extension, including children.
    Toward permanent residence
    No — indefinite temporary stay is not permanence. See the dead end on that question.
    Realistic timeline
    Immediate on arrival. Extensions take a few business days, and are usually handled through an agent.

    Verify this yourself before spending money

    Under an hour of work. This is the check that matters — not our word, and not an agency's.

    That the ordinary E-class visa is still being issued on arrival at your entry point

    Ask: Cambodian General Department of Immigration

    Check the official portal's visa-on-arrival page for your intended airport or land border, and confirm the class list includes the ordinary visa. www.evisa.gov.kh

    A real answer sounds like: The ordinary or business class listed by name, with a fee. Land borders sometimes differ from airports.

    What supporting documents your chosen extension class currently requires

    Ask: General Department of Immigration, or a reputable local visa agent

    Ask specifically: 'For a twelve-month EB extension in 2026, what supporting documents do you require from me and from my sponsor?' www.immigration.gov.kh

    A real answer sounds like: A concrete document list. Enforcement tightened in 2026, so an answer from 2023 forums is not reliable.

    Hard requirements

    • US passport valid at least 6 months 1
    • Ask for the ordinary or business visa at the counter, not the tourist one — They are different classes at different prices and the counter will issue whichever you ask for. 10

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    Ordinary E-class visa on arrivalAbout US$35Five dollars more than the tourist visa, and the only version that leads anywhere. 10
    Extension of stay, 1 monthAbout US$45 10
    Extension of stay, 3 monthsAbout US$80 10
    Extension of stay, 6 monthsAbout US$155 10
    Extension of stay, 12 monthsAbout US$285 to 300Requires a sponsor, and increasingly requires real supporting documents. 1011

    Step by step

    1. Ask for the ordinary visa at the airport counter

      Say 'ordinary visa' or 'business visa', not 'tourist visa'. This is the whole decision. 10

      Who: You Takes: Minutes

    2. Work out which extension class you qualify for before day 25

      EB for business and employment, EG while job-hunting, ER for retirement, ES for study. The class determines what documents you need.

      Who: You

      Blocked by: Do this in your first two weeks, not your last two days.

    3. Apply for the extension before the 30 days expire

      Most people use an agent; the immigration office also handles it directly. Have accommodation details and supporting documents ready. 2

      Who: You, usually via an agent Where: General Department of Immigration

    How this goes wrong

    Being given a tourist visa because you did not specify

    Consequence: You are on the dead-end class and will have to exit and re-enter.

    Avoid it: Say the words 'ordinary visa' at the counter and check the sticker before you walk away.

    Leaving the extension to the last few days

    Consequence: Rushed agent fees, or an overstay if documents are missing.

    Avoid it: Start the extension at around day 20.

    EB Extension plus Work Permit — employed

    EB moderate

    The standard route for anyone working for a Cambodian employer. Two documents from two ministries: the EB extension to stay, and the work permit to work. Both are required, and the calendar around them is unforgiving in a way that catches almost everyone once.

    Best for
    Anyone with a Cambodian employer, including local offices of foreign organisations, schools, and NGOs.
    You get
    EB extension up to 12 months; work permit valid to 31 December of the year of issue
    Renewable
    Yes, annually — but inside a fixed renewal window, not on your own anniversary.
    Work locally
    Yes, with the work permit. The EB extension alone is not work authorisation.
    Family
    Dependants extend on the EB class, sponsored by the same employer.
    Toward permanent residence
    No.
    Realistic timeline
    Work permits run on an annual cycle rather than a per-person one. Realistically 4 to 10 weeks from arrival to both documents in hand, dominated by US document legalization if any is needed.

    Verify this yourself before spending money

    Under an hour of work. This is the check that matters — not our word, and not an agency's.

    That your employer holds a current Foreign Manpower Quota with capacity

    Ask: Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training, via your employer's FWCMS account

    Ask HR to open their FWCMS account and show you the quota for the current year and how many places remain. Ask before you sign anything. www.fwcms.mlvt.gov.kh

    A real answer sounds like: A number of approved places and a number used. 'We'll sort it out' means they may not have applied in the September-to-November window.

    The exact work permit renewal deadline for the coming year

    Ask: Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training

    Confirm on the FWCMS portal that the renewal window is still 1 January to 31 March, and whether the permit expiry is still fixed at 31 December. www.fwcms.mlvt.gov.kh

    A real answer sounds like: Published dates. These are administrative deadlines that can move between years, so check annually rather than assuming.

    Which of your US documents actually need legalization

    Ask: Royal Embassy of Cambodia in Washington DC, and your employer

    Ask the employer which documents the labour ministry is requiring this year, then ask the embassy what the current legalization fee and turnaround is for that set. www.embassyofcambodiadc.org

    A real answer sounds like: A document list from the employer and a fee schedule from the embassy. Do not order legalization for documents nobody asked for.

    Hard requirements

    • A Cambodian employer to sponsor both documents — The employer files the work permit; you cannot obtain one on your own behalf as an employee. 12
    • Your employer holds a Foreign Manpower Quota for the year — Companies apply for the quota between 1 September and 30 November for the following year, capped at 10% of the Cambodian workforce. If your employer missed that window, your permit cannot be issued no matter how qualified you are. 13
    • Passport, recent patent tax certificate from the employer, health certificate, and a 4x6cm photo — The health check is done in Cambodia. The patent tax certificate is the employer's, not yours. 3
    • Legalized supporting documents where required — Degrees and background documents need the full three-step consular chain, not an apostille. 21

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    EB extension, 12 monthsAbout US$285 10
    Work permit and employment cardAbout US$100 to 200 per yearUsually paid by the employer. Confirm on the FWCMS portal at application time. 3
    US document legalization, three-step chainUS$200 to 600Per document set, including embassy fees and courier. Materially more than an apostille would cost. 21
    Health check in CambodiaUS$20 to 50

    Step by step

    1. Before accepting the job, ask about the quota

      Ask the employer directly whether they hold a Foreign Manpower Quota for the current year with room on it. This one question prevents the worst outcome on this pathway. 13

      Who: You

      Blocked by: Everything depends on this and it cannot be fixed mid-year.

    2. Enter on the ordinary E-class visa

      Not the tourist visa. 10

      Who: You

    3. Convert to the EB extension

      Your employer sponsors it. Twelve months is the usual target. 10

      Who: Employer, with you

    4. Complete the health check in Cambodia

      Quick and inexpensive, at a recognised clinic. 3

      Who: You Where: Cambodia

    5. Employer files the work permit on FWCMS

      All work permit and employment card applications run through the Foreign Workers Centralized Management System. 3

      Who: Your employer Where: fwcms.mlvt.gov.kh

    6. Diarise the renewal window immediately

      Permits are valid to 31 December regardless of when they were issued, and renewals are filed between 1 January and 31 March. Put both dates in your calendar the day you receive the permit. 311

      Who: You Takes: Two minutes now, saves the year

    How this goes wrong

    Joining an employer with no Foreign Manpower Quota

    Consequence: You cannot be issued a work permit at all this year. Either you work illegally or you wait until the next quota cycle.

    Avoid it: Ask before signing. This is the highest-value question on this entire pathway.

    Assuming the work permit runs twelve months from issue

    Consequence: A permit issued in October expires on 31 December, ten weeks later, and you file a renewal in January having barely used it.

    Avoid it: Understand that the permit year is a calendar year, not a personal one.

    Missing the 31 March renewal deadline

    Consequence: Penalties, and a period working without a valid permit during a year of increased compliance checks.

    Avoid it: Calendar it in January, not March.

    Getting an apostille instead of consular legalization

    Consequence: Documents rejected outright; four to eight weeks lost and the fees are not recoverable.

    Avoid it: Cambodia is not in the Apostille Convention. Three-step chain, every time.

    Own Company plus Self-Sponsored EB

    EB high

    Register a Cambodian company, and it becomes the sponsor for your own extension and work permit. Cambodia's company formation thresholds are far lower than Vietnam's investor tiers, which makes this the realistic self-directed route in the region — at the cost of real, permanent compliance obligations.

    Best for
    Consultants, small business owners, and remote workers who want a clean legal basis and are willing to run a real entity to get it.
    You get
    EB extension up to 12 months, renewable indefinitely
    Renewable
    Yes, while the company remains compliant and the patent tax is current.
    Work locally
    Yes, with a work permit sponsored by your own company.
    Family
    Dependants extend on the EB class sponsored by your company.
    Toward permanent residence
    No.
    Realistic timeline
    6 to 12 weeks to a registered company, then the normal EB and work permit cycle on top.

    Verify this yourself before spending money

    Under an hour of work. This is the check that matters — not our word, and not an agency's.

    The genuine all-in annual running cost of the company, not the formation quote

    Ask: Two or three Cambodian corporate service providers, independently

    Ask each for a written annual figure covering patent tax, monthly filings, annual return, and audit if applicable. Compare the three.

    A real answer sounds like: Three comparable annual figures. A provider who will only quote formation is quoting you the cheap half.

    That a company of your size can obtain a Foreign Manpower Quota covering its own foreign director

    Ask: Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training

    Ask your provider to confirm how the 10%-of-Cambodian-workforce cap is applied to a company whose only foreign worker is its owner, and what minimum local headcount that implies. www.fwcms.mlvt.gov.kh 13

    A real answer sounds like: A concrete answer about local headcount. This is the detail that decides whether a one-person company works.

    Hard requirements

    • A registered Cambodian company in good standing — With a current patent tax certificate — that certificate is a required document for the work permit application. 3
    • A Foreign Manpower Quota for your own company — The quota rule applies to your company too. Apply in the 1 September to 30 November window for the following year. 13
    • Ongoing monthly and annual tax filings — A Cambodian company files whether or not it trades. This is the real cost of the pathway and it never stops. 16

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    Company registrationUS$700 to 2,500 in professional feesVaries widely by provider and structure. Get more than one quote.
    Patent tax, annualFrom about US$100 per yearScales with declared turnover band. Required annually and required for the work permit.
    Accounting and compliance, annualUS$1,000 to 4,000 per yearThe cost people forget when comparing this against Vietnam's investor route.
    EB extension plus work permitAbout US$400 to 500 per year combined 103

    Step by step

    1. Decide whether you want a company or only want a visa

      If the answer is only a visa, price three years of accounting and filings before proceeding. A dormant company is a recurring bill and a recurring obligation.

      Who: You

      Blocked by: Make this decision before spending anything.

    2. Register the company and obtain the patent tax certificate

      The patent tax certificate is what the work permit application actually needs.

      Who: Your local corporate services provider Takes: 4 to 8 weeks

    3. Apply for your company's Foreign Manpower Quota in the correct window

      1 September to 30 November, for the following calendar year. Miss it and you cannot sponsor yourself next year. 13

      Who: You, as the company

    4. Sponsor your own EB extension and work permit

      Same FWCMS process as any employer. 3

      Who: Your company

    5. Set up real bookkeeping from month one

      Retrospective bookkeeping in Cambodia is expensive and unpleasant. Start correctly.

      Who: You and your accountant

    How this goes wrong

    Forming the company without checking the quota arithmetic for a one-person business

    Consequence: A registered company that cannot lawfully sponsor its own owner.

    Avoid it: Run the verification step above before registering, not after.

    Treating the company as a visa product and ignoring the filings

    Consequence: Penalties accumulate quietly, and the patent tax certificate you need for the work permit becomes unobtainable.

    Avoid it: Budget annual compliance from day one and pay it like rent.

    Missing the September-to-November quota window

    Consequence: No work permit next year, from your own company.

    Avoid it: It is an annual calendar item. Set it the day you incorporate.

    ER Retirement Extension

    ER low

    A genuine retirement route, which most of Cambodia's neighbours in this guide do not offer. Age 55 and over, evidence of retirement income, no local work. Renewable indefinitely in 1, 3, 6, or 12-month blocks.

    Best for
    Americans 55 and over living on Social Security, a pension, or savings, who want a low-cost base with genuinely simple paperwork.
    You get
    Extensions of 1, 3, 6, or 12 months
    Renewable
    Yes, indefinitely.
    Work locally
    No. The ER extension carries no right to work, and taking local work on it is illegal employment.
    Family
    A spouse generally extends on a dependant basis. Confirm the class for your circumstances.
    Toward permanent residence
    No.
    Realistic timeline
    A few weeks from arrival, most of which is assembling income evidence.

    Verify this yourself before spending money

    Under an hour of work. This is the check that matters — not our word, and not an agency's.

    What income evidence the immigration office is actually accepting this year, and whether any minimum figure is applied

    Ask: Cambodian General Department of Immigration, or the Cambodian embassy in Washington DC before you travel

    Ask: 'For an ER extension in 2026, what documents do you accept as proof of retirement income, and is there a minimum monthly figure?' Take the answer in writing if you can. www.immigration.gov.kh 6

    A real answer sounds like: A document list. If they decline to state a minimum figure, that is itself the answer — see the contested section — and you should over-evidence rather than aim at a rumoured threshold.

    Whether your spouse can extend alongside you and on what class

    Ask: General Department of Immigration

    Ask specifically about a spouse under 55, since the age gate applies to the ER holder. www.immigration.gov.kh

    A real answer sounds like: A named extension class for the spouse. Do not assume it is automatic.

    Hard requirements

    • Aged 55 or older — The core gate. Exceptional cases are sometimes described, but plan on the age rule. 614
    • Evidence you can support yourself without local employment — Pension statements, a Social Security benefit letter, or bank statements showing regular deposits. Commonly cited benchmarks sit around US$1,500 per month, but Cambodia does not publish an official minimum the way some neighbours do — see the contested claims section. 146
    • Evidence you are retired and not employed — A pension statement or Social Security entitlement letter usually serves both purposes. 14
    • Entry on the ordinary E-class visa — You enter on the ordinary visa and convert. You do not arrive on a retirement visa. 10

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    ER extension of stay, 12 monthsAbout US$275 14
    Ordinary E-class visa on entryAbout US$35 10
    Agent assistance, optionalUS$50 to 150Widely used and genuinely useful for this class, given how little official written guidance exists.

    Step by step

    1. Assemble income evidence before you fly

      A Social Security benefit letter, recent pension statements, and several months of bank statements. Get them in the US where obtaining them is easy.

      Who: You Takes: 1 to 3 weeks

      Blocked by: Far easier to obtain before you leave than after.

    2. Enter on the ordinary E-class visa

      Ask for the ordinary visa at the counter. 10

      Who: You

    3. Apply to convert to the ER extension

      Through the immigration office or a local agent, within your first 30 days. 14

      Who: You Where: General Department of Immigration

    4. Renew before expiry, indefinitely

      Twelve months at a time is usual once established.

      Who: You

    How this goes wrong

    Arriving on the tourist visa

    Consequence: You cannot convert to ER and must exit and re-enter.

    Avoid it: Ordinary E-class at the counter, always.

    Taking casual local work — teaching a few hours, helping at a friend's bar

    Consequence: Illegal employment during a year of increased compliance checks, with your extension class contradicting your activity.

    Avoid it: If you want to work, you want the EB and work permit route instead, whatever your age.

    Aiming exactly at a rumoured income threshold

    Consequence: Refusal, because no official figure is published and the assessment is discretionary.

    Avoid it: Over-evidence. Bring more documentation than you think is needed.

    EG Extension — job seekers and remote workers

    EG low

    The extension class for people who are not yet employed. Short EG extensions of 1 and 3 months do not require a sponsor, which makes this the most accessible long-stay mechanism in the region — and the closest thing Cambodia has to a remote worker route, with an important legal caveat.

    Best for
    Job hunters on the ground, people deciding whether to commit to Cambodia, and remote workers who understand the caveat below.
    You get
    1, 3, or 6 months; 12-month extensions require a sponsor
    Renewable
    Yes in practice, though repeated renewal without ever taking employment attracts more questions than it used to.
    Work locally
    No. EG is a permission to stay while seeking work, not to work. Whether it covers remote work for foreign clients is genuinely contested — read the contested section before relying on it.
    Family
    Each person extends individually.
    Toward permanent residence
    No.
    Realistic timeline
    Days, through an agent.

    Verify this yourself before spending money

    Under an hour of work. This is the check that matters — not our word, and not an agency's.

    Whether short EG extensions are still being granted without a sponsor

    Ask: General Department of Immigration, or two independent local visa agents

    Ask two agents separately: 'Can I get a one-month and a three-month EG extension in 2026 with no sponsor, and what documents do you need from me?' Compare the answers. www.immigration.gov.kh 15

    A real answer sounds like: Consistent answers from both. Divergence means the practice is shifting and you should assume the stricter version.

    Whether working remotely for foreign clients requires a Cambodian work permit

    Ask: Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training

    Ask whether a foreign national residing in Cambodia and performing services solely for clients outside Cambodia, paid outside Cambodia, requires a work permit. www.fwcms.mlvt.gov.kh

    A real answer sounds like: Probably not a clean answer — which is exactly why this is in the contested section. Record whatever you are told and who told you.

    Hard requirements

    • Entry on the ordinary E-class visa 10
    • For 1 and 3-month extensions, no sponsor required — This is the unusual feature. Longer extensions require a Cambodian employer or a locally registered company. 1015
    • For 12-month extensions, a sponsor — Either an employer or a registered company. Umbrella arrangements through agents exist and vary in quality and legality — treat them with care. 15

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    EG extension, 1 monthAbout US$45 10
    EG extension, 3 monthsAbout US$80 10
    EG extension, 6 monthsAbout US$155 10
    EG extension, 12 monthsAbout US$285 to 300, plus whatever a sponsor costs 10

    Step by step

    1. Enter on the ordinary E-class visa

      As always, not the tourist class. 10

      Who: You

    2. Take a short EG extension while you establish yourself

      One or three months, no sponsor needed. This buys you time to find either a job or a clearer basis. 152

      Who: You

    3. Decide within that window what your real basis will be

      EG is a bridge, not a destination. Employment, your own company, or retirement if you qualify.

      Who: You

      Blocked by: Do not drift on repeated short extensions for years without deciding.

    4. Read the contested claim on remote work before relying on EG for it

      This is the specific point where Cambodia's reputation for permissiveness and its actual law diverge.

      Who: You

    How this goes wrong

    Treating EG as a de facto digital nomad visa with no further thought

    Consequence: You may be working without a permit, in a year when compliance checks have increased.

    Avoid it: Read the contested claim, decide deliberately, and revisit it as enforcement changes.

    Buying a 12-month sponsored extension from an agent without asking who the sponsor is

    Consequence: Your legal status depends on a company you have never seen, which may not be compliant itself.

    Avoid it: If you are being sponsored, know exactly which registered entity is sponsoring you.

    Rolling short EG extensions for years

    Consequence: Increasing scrutiny at each renewal, and no accumulated status to show for the time.

    Avoid it: Use EG as a bridge with a decision date attached.

    ES Student Extension

    ES low

    For enrolment at a recognised Cambodian institution, including Khmer language programs. Inexpensive, low-friction, and a legitimate way to hold clear status while you work out whether Cambodia is right for you.

    Best for
    Younger movers, language learners, and anyone who wants an unambiguous basis for a first year.
    You get
    Aligned to the program, in the usual 1, 3, 6, or 12-month extension blocks
    Renewable
    Yes, while enrolled.
    Work locally
    No.
    Family
    Limited. Do not plan a family move around this class.
    Toward permanent residence
    No.
    Realistic timeline
    Weeks, once enrolled.

    Verify this yourself before spending money

    Under an hour of work. This is the check that matters — not our word, and not an agency's.

    That the school actually sponsors ES extensions

    Ask: The institution, and the General Department of Immigration

    Ask the school how many ES extensions they supported in the past year and ask to speak to a current foreign student. Then confirm with immigration that the school is recognised for this purpose. www.immigration.gov.kh

    A real answer sounds like: A number and a student contact. Vagueness means they expect you to arrange your own status, in which case you are really on the EG pathway.

    Hard requirements

    • Enrolment at a recognised institution — Universities and established language schools. Ask the school directly whether they sponsor ES extensions and how many they did last year. 10
    • Entry on the ordinary E-class visa 10

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    Khmer language program tuitionUS$300 to 1,500 per yearVaries enormously. Universities cost more.
    ES extensionSame schedule as other extensions, about US$80 for 3 months to US$285 for 12 10

    Step by step

    1. Confirm the school can sponsor before paying tuition

      This is the whole risk on this pathway.

      Who: You

      Blocked by: Do not pay first.

    2. Enter on the ordinary E-class visa

      Ask for the ordinary or business visa at the counter, never the tourist class — the ES conversion needs it. 10

      Who: You

    3. Convert to the ES extension with the school's enrolment documents

      Bring the school’s enrolment letter and your accommodation details. Do this inside your first 30 days. 2

      Who: You, with the school Where: General Department of Immigration

    How this goes wrong

    Paying a year of tuition to a school that cannot sponsor

    Consequence: Tuition spent and no status gained.

    Avoid it: Confirm sponsorship in writing before paying.

    Taking paid work on ES status

    Consequence: Illegal employment exposure.

    Avoid it: Keep income sources outside Cambodia, or move to the EB and work permit route.

    Citizenship by Investment or Donation

    very high

    Cambodia runs a real, published citizenship-by-investment program — a meaningful contrast with the regional trend of announcing golden visas that never launch. It is expensive, it is faster than most, and the headline figure is not the real cost.

    Best for
    People for whom a second passport, not merely residence, is the actual objective, and for whom roughly a third of a million dollars is a considered expense.
    You get
    Citizenship, with dual nationality permitted
    Renewable
    Not applicable.
    Work locally
    Yes, as a citizen.
    Family
    Family applications are contemplated; costs are per applicant and add up quickly.
    Toward permanent residence
    It is the only published route in this guide that leads to permanence.
    Realistic timeline
    Commonly reported at 3 to 6 months from submission to passport.

    Verify this yourself before spending money

    Under an hour of work. This is the check that matters — not our word, and not an agency's.

    The current legal instrument, thresholds, and whether the program is open today

    Ask: Independent Cambodian counsel you retain directly — not the agent selling you the program

    Ask them to name the law or sub-decree the program operates under and confirm the current donation and investment figures in writing. www.immigration.gov.kh

    A real answer sounds like: A named instrument and current figures. An adviser who cannot name the instrument is not advising you, they are selling to you.

    Whether all-in costs match what the agent quoted

    Ask: A second, unaffiliated agent or law firm

    Get a competing written quote for the identical outcome and compare line by line.

    A real answer sounds like: Two comparable quotes. Large divergence is a reason to slow down, not to pick the cheaper.

    Hard requirements

    • Donation of US$245,000 to the government, or a qualifying investment of at least US$305,000 — All-in costs including fees are commonly reported at roughly US$330,000 or more per applicant. 19
    • Aged 18 or over with no criminal record 19
    • Three visits to Cambodia during the process — For documentation, government submission, and passport collection. There is no prior residency requirement. 19

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    Donation routeUS$245,000 19
    Investment routeFrom US$305,000 19
    Fees, agents, and processingFrequently bringing the all-in total to US$330,000+Get a written all-in figure before committing to anything. 19

    Step by step

    1. Get a written all-in quote, not the headline figure

      Donation or investment amount, government fees, agent fees, legal fees, translation and legalization, and travel. One number.

      Who: You

      Blocked by: Do not proceed on a headline number.

    2. Verify the current legal basis independently

      The framework is actively evolving. Confirm the instrument and the current thresholds before transferring funds.

      Who: You, with independent counsel not paid by the agent

    3. Understand the US tax consequences before acquiring a second nationality

      Acquiring another citizenship does not end US tax obligations. Take US tax advice first. 8

      Who: Your US tax adviser

    4. Complete the three required visits

      For documentation, government submission, and passport collection. Plan them into your calendar and budget; there is no prior residency requirement but the visits are not optional. 19

      Who: You

    How this goes wrong

    Budgeting the headline donation figure

    Consequence: A shortfall of US$85,000 or more against the real all-in cost, discovered mid-process.

    Avoid it: Written all-in quote, before anything.

    Relying entirely on the agent selling the program

    Consequence: No independent check on an evolving legal framework, with a third of a million dollars committed.

    Avoid it: Retain your own counsel. On a purchase this size the fee is rounding.

    Assuming a second passport reduces US tax obligations

    Consequence: It does not. US citizens are taxed on worldwide income regardless of other nationalities held.

    Avoid it: Take US tax advice before, not after.

    Ten traps

    Cross-cutting failures that belong to no single pathway. If you read only one section of this guide, read this one.

    1An apostille is the wrong document for Cambodia

    expensive

    The trap. Cambodia is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention. Americans reflexively order an apostille because that is what works nearly everywhere, and it is rejected. The correct chain is Secretary of State certification for state-issued documents, then US Department of State authentication, then Cambodian Embassy legalization.

    Do this instead. Order the three-step consular legalization, and budget six to ten weeks and US$200 to 600 per document set. If you are comparing Cambodia against Vietnam, note that Vietnam moved to apostilles on 11 September 2026 and Cambodia did not — the two countries now need different paperwork. 215

    2The five-dollar decision at the airport counter

    trip ending

    The trap. The tourist visa is about US$30 and extends exactly once. The ordinary E-class visa is about US$35 and extends indefinitely into every long-stay class in this guide. The counter issues whichever you ask for, and most arrivals ask for the tourist visa because it is called the tourist visa.

    Do this instead. Say 'ordinary visa' or 'business visa' at the counter, and check the sticker before walking away. If you are even slightly unsure how long you will stay, pay the extra five dollars. 10

    3Your work permit expires on 31 December no matter when you got it

    expensive

    The trap. Work permits run on the calendar year, not on a twelve-month clock from issue. A permit issued in October expires on 31 December, and the renewal is filed between 1 January and 31 March.

    Do this instead. The day you receive the permit, put 31 December and 31 March in your calendar. If you are joining an employer late in the year, ask whether it is worth waiting for the new permit year. 311

    4The Foreign Manpower Quota is applied for a year in advance

    trip ending

    The trap. Companies must apply for their Foreign Manpower Quota between 1 September and 30 November for the following year, capped at 10% of their Cambodian workforce. If your prospective employer missed that window, you cannot be issued a work permit that year regardless of your qualifications.

    Do this instead. Ask any prospective employer, before signing, whether they hold a current quota with capacity remaining. Ask to see it in their FWCMS account. 13

    5The business visa is not permission to work

    trip ending

    The trap. Cambodia runs two documents from two ministries: the EB extension from the Ministry of Interior for the right to stay, and the work permit from the Ministry of Labour for the right to work. Holding EB while working without a permit is illegal employment, and 2026 has brought more frequent business compliance checks and substantial fines.

    Do this instead. Treat them as two separate obligations with two separate deadlines. Never assume the visa agent who got your EB also handled the work permit — ask explicitly. 1112

    6Badly bound documents are rejected on sight

    annoying

    The trap. The Cambodian Embassy requires multi-page documents to be securely bound with a paging seal or embossed seal. A stapled or loose multi-page document is rejected instantly, and you start the chain again.

    Do this instead. Confirm binding requirements with the embassy before submitting, and use a legalization service that has done Cambodia specifically rather than a generic apostille shop. 21

    7You cannot own land, and the workarounds carry real risk

    expensive

    The trap. Foreigners cannot own land in Cambodia. You can own a condominium unit under a strata title, but only above the ground floor and only within a 70% foreign cap per building. For anything landed, the routes are long leases, a Cambodian-majority company, or a licensed trustee. Nominee arrangements — the land in a Cambodian friend's name — remain common and are exactly as risky as they sound.

    Do this instead. Rent for at least a year. If you do buy, buy a strata-titled unit and verify the title is registered with the Ministry of Land Management. Get independent counsel who is not connected to the seller or the agent. 20

    8Cambodia's permissiveness is being quietly tightened

    expensive

    The trap. The country's reputation was built on extensions granted with minimal paperwork. In 2026, extensions increasingly require genuine supporting documents, accommodation records, and in some cases work permit or business proof, and compliance checks at businesses are more frequent.

    Do this instead. Do not plan on advice from forum posts more than a year or two old. Verify current requirements with two independent local agents before each renewal, and keep your paperwork genuinely in order rather than nominally. 1110

    9Old or damaged US banknotes are refused

    annoying

    The trap. Cambodia is dollarized, which is a real convenience, but notes that are torn, heavily marked, or from older series are routinely rejected by shops and even banks. Meanwhile change under a dollar comes back in riel.

    Do this instead. Bring crisp, recent notes. Inspect notes you are given as change, and refuse damaged ones at the point of transaction rather than discovering the problem later.

    10Your US licence may not convert to the class you actually need

    trip ending

    The trap. Conversion at MPWT produces an equivalent class only, and classes C, D and E cannot be converted to the same class. As in much of the region, the practical risk is riding a motorbike on a licence that does not cover it, then discovering after an accident that insurance declines.

    Do this instead. Convert your licence properly, obtain the motorbike class if you intend to ride, and get written confirmation from your health and travel insurers that they cover motorbike use at your licence class. 422

    Where the sources disagree

    Questions credible sources answer differently. We publish the disagreement rather than picking a side and hoping — a guide that hides a genuine conflict is more dangerous than one that names it.

    Does Cambodia tax a resident's foreign-sourced income?

    Position 1

    Yes. Residents — anyone present more than 182 days in the tax year — are taxed on worldwide salary income at progressive rates up to 20%, with a foreign tax credit available for tax paid abroad. 1617

    Held by: Professional tax guidance, including major-firm country summaries

    Position 2

    In practice, no. Cambodia's tax administration focuses almost exclusively on locally registered companies and formal local employment, and foreigners on foreign payrolls are effectively outside the net. 18

    Held by: Widely repeated expat and nomad tax commentary

    What this actually means for you. These describe the law and the enforcement pattern respectively, and both are probably accurate descriptions of their own subject. That means you are not choosing between two facts, you are choosing how much enforcement risk to carry. The exposure grows the longer you stay, the more visible your local footprint becomes, and the more the administration modernises.

    How to settle it for your own case. Get a written opinion from a Cambodian tax adviser for your specific facts — where you are paid, by whom, and for work performed where. Ask specifically whether they would file a return for someone in your position, and what happens if the position is later challenged. This costs a few hundred dollars and is the only way to convert a rumour into a position you can defend. 1618

    Does working remotely for foreign clients from Cambodia require a Cambodian work permit?

    Position 1

    Yes, arguably. The work permit regime covers foreigners working in Cambodia, and the labour authorities have not carved out remote work for foreign employers. Work performed physically in Cambodia is work in Cambodia. 1211

    Held by: A conservative reading of the labour regime

    Position 2

    In practice, no. Enforcement targets businesses employing foreigners locally, and the EG extension exists precisely for people who are in Cambodia without a local employer. 15

    Held by: Established expat practice and the design of the EG class

    What this actually means for you. Cambodia is materially more permissive here than Vietnam, but permissiveness is not permission. The 2026 tightening was aimed at businesses rather than individuals, which is why this remains unsettled rather than resolved.

    How to settle it for your own case. If the risk matters to you, remove it structurally: register a company and sponsor your own work permit, which is far cheaper here than the equivalent in Vietnam. If you accept the risk, at least accept it knowingly, and revisit the question at every renewal. 1215

    Is there a minimum income requirement for the ER retirement extension?

    Position 1

    Around US$1,500 per month is the working benchmark, and applicants should evidence at least that. 14

    Held by: Most published expat guidance

    Position 2

    There is no official published minimum. Cambodia does not publish a figure the way several neighbouring countries do; the requirement is to show you can support yourself without local employment, assessed with discretion. 614

    Held by: Official and semi-official descriptions of the ER class

    What this actually means for you. Because the assessment is discretionary rather than arithmetic, aiming precisely at a rumoured threshold is the wrong strategy. More evidence is strictly better, and the form of the evidence matters as much as the amount.

    How to settle it for your own case. Ask the immigration office or the Cambodian embassy directly what they accept, and bring more documentation than any published figure suggests: benefit letter, pension statements, and several months of bank statements. 614

    Eight phases, in order. These apply whichever pathway you took; items marked with a pathway only appear for that route. Your ticks are saved in this browser.

    Decide and pressure-test

    T-120 to T-60 days

    Cambodia's low barrier to entry cuts both ways: it is easy to arrive and easy to drift. Decide what you are doing before you land.

    Assemble and legalize documents

    T-120 to T-45 days

    The single biggest difference from most other countries: Cambodia does not accept apostilles. Read this before you order anything.

    T-90 to T-0 days

    Identical in structure to any US departure, with one Cambodia-specific tax question you must settle yourself.

    Money and banking

    T-45 to T+30 days

    The good news: Cambodia is dollarized, which removes most of the currency friction of a move to Asia.

    One decision at the airport counter shapes everything that follows.

    First 90 days

    T+7 to T+90 days

    Staying legal, year after year

    Continuous

    Cambodia's annual cycle is unusual: it runs on fixed calendar dates, not on your personal anniversary. This is where people get caught.

    Contingency and exit

    Have this before you need it

    Written while things are going well.

    What we are watching

    Rules that are moving, or expected to. Each carries the date we next check it. When one lands, this guide is updated and you get the new edition — that is what your purchase actually buys beyond the first read.

    The 2026 tightening of extension and compliance requirements

    Enforcement shifting Impact if it lands: pathway changing We re-check by December 1, 2026

    If documentation requirements for extensions keep rising, the EG bridge narrows and Cambodia stops being the region's easy option. The reality check and the EG pathway would both need rewriting. 1110

    Affects: Ordinary (E-class) Visa — the gateway, EG Extension — job seekers and remote workers, EB Extension plus Work Permit — employed

    Citizenship-by-investment framework and thresholds

    In force, details unclear Impact if it lands: significant We re-check by December 1, 2026

    Thresholds and the governing instrument are described as actively evolving. Any change alters the only permanence route in this pack. 19

    Affects: Citizenship by Investment or Donation

    Work permit renewal window and quota dates for the next cycle

    In force, details unclear Impact if it lands: significant We re-check by November 15, 2026

    The 1 January to 31 March renewal window and the 1 September to 30 November quota window are administrative dates that can move between years. They drive the most consequential deadlines in this pack. 313

    Affects: EB Extension plus Work Permit — employed, Own Company plus Self-Sponsored EB

    Tax administration reach over foreign-sourced individual income

    In force, details unclear Impact if it lands: significant We re-check by January 15, 2027

    If the General Department of Taxation begins assessing resident foreigners on foreign-source income, the first contested claim resolves and the money module needs a substantial rewrite. 1618

    Cambodia's position on the Apostille Convention

    In force, details unclear Impact if it lands: minor We re-check by March 1, 2027

    Cambodia remains outside the Convention. Vietnam's accession in September 2026 makes this a live comparison, and any Cambodian move would simplify the documents module considerably. 21
